data.body:
EPIC PLAN REVIEW #4 -> BLOCK, 1 blocking. Pass-3's jira_fields/pinned-import blocker RESOLVED (symbol-split + contract parameterization accepted). The new blocker is a sharp catch on MY OWN remediation #2/#3 wording.
BLOCKER (G6): I had written that J2 unifies the value maps 'preserving each caller's current observable behavior'. That is IMPOSSIBLE for the 'deleted' key, because the two callers currently DISAGREE: outbound_fields maps deleted->Done; jira_fields omits it and falls through to status.replace('_',' ').title() -> 'Deleted'. One unified dict cannot preserve both. The reviewer was right and my phrasing was incoherent.
REMEDIATION #4 — decided it explicitly instead of deferring. Investigation found a THIRD copy: rebar_reconciler/config.py:37 local_to_jira_status ALSO maps deleted->Done. So 2 of 3 copies agree on Done, and the ACLI omission is the outlier. Further, 'Deleted' is NOT a state in the live DIG workflow ({To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}), so that transition would be REJECTED by Jira — a latent bug, not behavior worth preserving. And 'deleted' IS a real TicketStatus (src/rebar/types.py:21), so the path is reachable, not dead.
 - J2 now adopts 'deleted': 'Done' as THE ONE DECLARED observable change in an otherwise behavior-preserving story, called out explicitly rather than smuggled, pinned by its own test.
 - Kept the ACLI .title() fallback: it is independently load-bearing because transition_issue accepts EITHER a local status name OR an already-Jira name ('In Progress' passes through it unchanged). Only the deleted outcome changes.
 - Epic text corrected from 'two copies' to three, naming config.py:37, and scoping config.py's copy OUT (engine-level config = wider blast radius than the adapter seam).
 - Also fixed a structural slip of my own: the probe/RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES paragraph had landed BETWEEN two bullets of the movable/stays-put list, breaking it. Moved after the list.
 - Commented the narrowed scope onto bug fe15: J2 owns the deleted decision; fe15 retains (a) the missing ACLI-side characterization pins — the original finding, and (b) folding config.py's third copy in.
